title: BitNN: A Bit-Serial Accelerator for K-Nearest Neighbor Search in Point Clouds
problem: Point cloud kNN search suffers from low efficiency in Euclidean distance computation operations due to unnecessary computations and varying data precision requirements. Existing acceleration techniques overlook operation-level optimization opportunities.
motivation: kNN search is an important kernel for point cloud-based machine perception applications which have achieved widespread success.
method: BitNN computes the distance between points one bit at a time (bit-serial computation) rather than computing the entire distance at once. The hardware uses dimension-wise point cloud encoding (organizing all x-coordinates together, all y-coordinates together, and so on) and point-wise data layout (grouping each point's three coordinates together) to enable adaptive precision processing, where the system adjusts how many bits it needs to compute based on the data. It employs an early termination mechanism: after computing just the first few bits of a distance, it estimates a lower bound on the final distance, and if that lower bound already exceeds the best distance found so far, it stops computing that distance entirely, eliminating unnecessary operations. The hardware accelerator exploits massive parallelism to run thousands of these bit-serial distance calculations simultaneously, improving computing efficiency.
key_novelty: Computing distance bit by bit instead of all at once enables early stopping and adaptive precision, which significantly reduces unnecessary computation.
contributions: Bit-serial computation method for recursive Euclidean distance calculation in kNN search
Dimension-wise encoding and point-wise layout for adaptive precision processing
Early termination mechanism based on distance lower bound estimation
Efficient bit-serial accelerator architecture exploiting massive parallelism

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 3.6x power efficiency (vs comparable architecture), 2.9x (integrated into ParallelNN)
